reviews.review:
Game is bad. Straight up.
It's a buggy mess: controls barely work, the phone texting is incredibly broken and unpolished, and at some point i just stopped being able to interact with boxes making the progression impossible even on a reload.
It isn't a horror game and isn't scary: the devs say "no cheap jumpscares" and it is "all atmosphere" and yet there is literally no tension or stakes. The scariest thing in the game is the state of the dump you work in, and the miracle that it somehow is still open.

Lastly, the game is FULL - AND I MEAN FULL - of AI.
Say what you want about AI gen, good or bad. But the dev EXPLICITLY SAYS IN THE AI DISCLOSURE that this game "uses generative AI in a limited way to create rough bases for some 2D art and music". Their words not mine.
This entire game is filled with unfiltered AI, unedited in any way, including mispelled and brain-rot-esque posters, employee portraits, and the most annoying music you have ever heard.

Overall, the game is slop and charging $9 cad (full-price) for this is actually insane in the indie horror genre.
reviews.developer_response:
Hey thanks for taking the time to write this, even if the experience wasn’t great for you.

On the gameplay issues: we haven’t been able to reproduce the specific problems you described (controls not working, phone texting flow being blocked, or progression feeling impossible), and we haven’t seen widespread reports of them but if something broke on your run, we absolutely want to track it down. If you’re willing, could you share a short gameplay clip showing what happens when you try to progress (and roughly what part of the game you’re at)? Even 30–60 seconds helps a lot. If you remember any exact steps that led to it (loading a save, doing X then Y, etc.), that’s even better.

On the AI note: for transparency, AI was used only in a limited way to help with some 2D art and music assets. The game’s code, scripting, logic, gameplay systems, and implementation were done solely by us not AI.

And on the horror: the game is a slow-burn — the more intense/scary moments ramp up later as you progress, so if you didn’t get very far, you may not have reached the parts where it really hits.

Either way, thanks again for giving Late Hours a shot. We’re actively supporting it and want it running right for everyone.

— Yas & Miguel
